verdictBasis: Every dispatched attack on custody, digests, fixture bytes, platform quotation, protocol quotation, closure bits, last-heading custody, speaker naming, and landing status fails: the subject sits at its dispatched sha256 and mode 0444, all 42 path-to-digest pairs load-equal live bytes, the four copies are distinct regular 0444 four-byte ffffffff files with no Windows copy, all three dispatched landed findings are present, and no protected anchor was remasured or recorded as current. One residual wording defect lands. doesNot[47] still asserts '8 unlabeled Claude observation strings'. No Claude review cited anywhere in the subject has eight observations: the g21-fixture-corpus.v22 Claude Stage A review has five, the g21-fixture-corpus.v23 Claude Stage A review has six. The figure 8 is the surviving fragment of the exact false count that live CLAUDE-G21FXV23-M-1 and CLAUDE-G21FXV23-M-2 and the live unlabeled Codex g21-fixture-corpus.v23 MUST-FIX all measured against the predecessor. It is one SHOULD-FIX rather than a MUST-FIX because the dispatched landing that M-2 defines is present and exact, the operative prohibition the clause states is honoured everywhere in the file, and the true counts are stated correctly at two other sites in the same subject.

findings.title: doesNot[47] still asserts 8 unlabeled Claude observation strings, a count no cited live review supports.
findings.measurement: The clause reads 'Does not invent observation identifiers for the 8 unlabeled Claude observation strings.' It is the only surviving occurrence of the string '8 unlabeled' in the subject. Every Claude review the subject cites was counted from live bytes: g21-fixture-corpus.v23 has 6 observations, g21-fixture-corpus.v22 has 5, g21-fixture-corpus.v21 has 9, g21-fixture-corpus.v20 has 9, g21-fixture-corpus.v19 has 9, leftover-join.v25 of G21 has 5, leftover-join.v20 of G21 has 2. None has 8, and no pair sums to 8. The clause is carried verbatim from g21-fixture-corpus.v23 doesNot[47], where the 8 came from the predecessor's now-deleted findingDisposition.claudeV22Observations. Live CLAUDE-G21FXV23-M-2 named that count explicitly among the four wrong elements ('the observation count (5, not 8)'), and the live unlabeled Codex g21-fixture-corpus.v23 MUST-FIX recorded the same candidateSummary 'ACCEPT 0/0; 8 unlabeled observations' as unsupported. The subject repaired the count at basedOn.predecessorV22.reviews.claude.verdict (5) and at findingDisposition.claudeV23Observations (6) but left this one site unrevised.
findings.whyShouldFix: doesNot is a current-standing clause set that would enter the register with this candidate. The clause asserts a fact about live predecessor review bytes that no reader can reproduce from disk, and it is the last fragment of the very count two independent Stage A reviewers rejected one version ago. Carrying it forward re-enters a refuted number into the successor that was dispatched to remove it.
findings.whyNotMustFix: The dispatched landing for CLAUDE-G21FXV23-M-2 is the restatement of the predecessorV22 Claude verdict from live bytes, and that is present and exact, so M-2 is landed as dispatched. The operative prohibition the clause states, that no observation identifier is invented, holds without exception: a sweep of the subject finds zero observation identifiers for any predecessor observation string, and the count is a descriptive qualifier on a prohibition rather than the prohibition itself. The correct counts are stated at two other sites in the same file. No digest, mode, fixture byte, platform, recording status, leftover partition, closure bit, last-heading custody, readiness status or operative authority is false under this defect.
findings.requiredFix: In a frozen successor, write doesNot[47] without the unbacked count, or with the count restated from live bytes. Either 'Does not invent observation identifiers for the unlabeled Claude observation strings.' or a count that matches the review being referred to, 6 for the g21-fixture-corpus.v23 Claude Stage A review. Do not edit this frozen subject, its copies, or any predecessor.
